body:
I'm a bit puzzled by the usage of `p_signal`.

Would you be able to elaborate for me what it's doing here?

I believe this gets pointer to the `HashMap<StringName, SignalData> signal_map` defined in `object.h`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/230e6bfc3b59a3363d25d65a2febf0610d750688/core/object/object.h#L643

...which, then, is checked if it is null. If not, the defined class is checked if it has the signal with `p_signal` name.

I think this is for the direct access to signals. Remember you can access to `$Button.pressed.connect(function)` instead of `$Button.connect("pressed", function)`.

This is why (again, I think) this requires `p_signal`. Because, otherwise, how would GDScript know whether this is `button_up`, `button_down`, `pressed` or `toggled`?

> If not, the defined class is checked if it has the signal with p_signal name.

Sorry, I reread your function and I think might need a bit more context. I'm not sure I understand the reason for checking if the object has a `p_signal` signal. Why is that the case?
